subject: WCOM
title: Public Speaking
description: Introduction to the principles of argumentation, organization, and delivery of public speech. History of the role of public speech in democratic society. Practice of public speaking as a skill.

subject: WCOM
title: Critical Analysis and Composition
description: Principles of effective written communication: audience, purpose, organization, and style. Emphasis on short writing assignments leading to the composition of longer essays. Critical analysis of academic and popular genres. Application of rhetorical strategies. Pre-writing and re-writing processes. Multiple drafts and peer review.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CEAP 150.

subject: WCOM
title: Writing in the Social Sciences
description: Introduces the analytical, research-oriented, and evidence-based writing practices common to the socials ciences. Focus on genres such as research reports, policy briefs, data commentaries, and structured arguments grounded in empirical evidence. Emphasizes disciplinary conventions, the use of sources, and rhetorical strategies within the social sciences. Early engagement with the writing demands of research-driven disciplines.

subject: WCOM
title: Academic Skills
description: An introduction to producing university-level academic writing and oral presentations that incorporate research synthesis, well-supported arguments, and reliable evidence. Topics include metacognitive skills, note-taking strategies, ethical use of Artificial Intelligence/Large Language Models, and other strategies to support learner autonomy.

subject: WCOM
title: Communication in Management 1
description: Written and oral communication in Management (in English): emphasis on strategies for identifying, analyzing, and solving writing and speaking problems. Course work based on academic and professional communication in management.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CCOM 205.

notes: Because this course uses a workshop format, attendance at first class is desirable.
Continuing Studies: requirement for the EA, AAC, and the Canadian Institute of Management.

subject: WCOM
title: Introduction to Creative Writing
description: Production of original creative works in English. Study and application of writing techniques and craft elements observed in both traditional and contemporary forms, ranging from poetic forms such as the sonnet, the villanelle, and free verse,to short fiction forms such as the short story and the vignette, to hybrid forms such as prose poetry and flash fiction. Craft, analysis of literary texts, workshop-style critique, and multiple drafts.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CCOM 200.

subject: WCOM
title: Communication in Engineering
description: Written and oral communication in Engineering (in English): strategies for generating, developing, organizing, and presenting ideas in a technical setting; problem-solving; communicating to different audiences; editing and revising; and public speaking. Course work based on academic, technical, and professional writing in engineering.

restrictions.text: Only open to students in Engineering degree programs.

subject: WCOM
title: ESL: Foundations of Academic English
description: Focus on core academic English competencies at the intermediate level, including sentence structure, grammar, cohesion, paragraph development, and academic vocabulary. Introduces short academic texts and foundational writing and communication practices, alongside strategies for note-taking, vocabulary building, editing, and oral presentation structure. Provides essential linguistic skills for engaging in academic communication and more advanced writing contexts.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CESL 200. Open only to students in degree programs.

subject: WCOM
title: ESL: Academic Writing and Communication Competencies
description: Focus on upper-intermediate academic English competencies through extended paragraphing, short essays, and genre-based writing. Emphasizes academic vocabulary development, grammatical accuracy in common academic structures, rhetorical organization, and effective communication across academic contexts.Foundational source integration and presentation skills in more complex university-level writing and communicative tasks.

prerequisites.text: CESL 200 or WCOM 225 or placement test.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CESL 300. Only open to students in degree programs.

subject: WCOM
title: ESL: Essay and Critical Thinking
description: Academic writing skills and communicative competence in English at the upper-intermediate level. Critical thinking and reading applied to the whole writing process. Focus on integrating sources, creating effective arguments, and understanding essay structure and paragraph essentials. Academic genres: summary, paraphrase, quotation, and critique. Review of writing mechanics and grammar.

prerequisites.text: CESL 300 or WCOM 235 or placement test.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CESL 400. Only open to students in degree programs.

subject: WCOM
title: Research Essay and Rhetoric
description: Academic research-based writing across the disciplines. Article summary, critical analysis, rhetorical strategies, citation and paraphrase of academic sources, and editing for cohesion and clarity.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CESL 500 or CEAP 250 or WCOM 255. Only open to students in degree programs - all years and faculties.

notes: Intended for students whose first language is English.
Entrance test: Short essay first day of classes.

subject: WCOM
title: ESL: Research Essay and Rhetoric
description: Principles and use of academic research skills to generate academic writing at an advanced level of English across the disciplines. Focus on article summary, critical analysis, and logical reasoning to develop sound arguments and well-reasoned essays. Common rhetorical strategies, citation and paraphrase of academic sources, and editing skills to enhance cohesion and avoid common English-as-a-Second Language (ESL) errors in grammar, syntax, and vocabulary.

prerequisites.text: CESL 400 or WCOM 245 or placement test.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CEAP 250 or CESL 500. Only open to students in degree programs.

subject: WCOM
title: ESL: Academic Skills
description: The university classroom: note-taking and summary of lectures; paraphrase and summary of written and multimedia materials; oral and seminar presentations; ethical use of Artificial Intelligence/Large Language Models. Critical thinking, reading, writing, listening, and speaking skills and strategies.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CESL 299.

notes: **Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop, and withdrawal deadlines do not apply. Add/drop is the fourth lecture day and withdrawal with financial penalty is the fifth lecture day.
Although this course follows a MTWR class schedule pattern, the last day of class may be on a Friday.

subject: WCOM
title: Writing and Community Action
description: Exploration of the relationship between experiential writing and community engagement. Instruction in and application of principles of writing pedagogy (in English) and best practices in community leadership.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CCOM 300.

notes: On-site facilitation (1.5 hours per week) of small-group writing events at community organizations and associations.

subject: WCOM
title: Writing Poetry
description: Production of original works of literary poetry in English. Advanced study and application ofwriting techniques,craft elements, poetic approaches and formal considerations used in contemporary free verse. In-depth instruction in the nuanced use of sound, line, image, rhythm, figurative language, and form. Craft, analysis of modern and contemporary literary poems, workshop-style critique, multiple drafts, and substantive revision.

prerequisites.text: CCOM 200 or WCOM 203 or permission of the Centre.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CCOM 321.

subject: WCOM
title: Communicating Science
description: Production of written and oral assignments (in English) designed to communicate scientific problems and findings to varied audiences Analysis of the disciplinary conventions of scientific discourse in terms of audience, purpose, organization, and style; comparative rhetorical analysis of academic and popular genres, including abstracts, lab reports, research papers, print and online journalism.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CCOM 314.

subject: WCOM
title: Writing the Internet
description: Critical assessment of digital genres in terms of audience, purpose, organization, and style; application of rhetorical strategies for effective communication in digital contexts in English. Topics and readings derived from writing pedagogy and critical analyses of online environments: technological affordances, non-linear structure, “living” texts, online identity, network dynamics, authorial collaboration.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CCOM 315.

subject: WCOM
title: Writing Short Fiction
description: Production of original works of literary short fiction in English. Advanced study and application of written storytelling techniques and craft elements used in contemporary short fiction forms, with a main focus on the short story. In-depth instruction in the nuanced creation of character, dialogue, scene, setting, point of view, narrative distance, and structure. Craft, analysis of published literary short fiction, workshopstyle critique, multiple drafts, and substantive revision.

prerequisites.text: CCOM 200 or WCOM 203 or permission of the Centre.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CCOM 322.

subject: WCOM
title: Writing Creative Nonfiction
description: Production of original works of literary creative nonfiction in English. Advanced study and application of story telling techniques and craft elements used in forms such as the memoir essay, literary journalism, and the lyric essay. In-depth instruction in the nuanced use of structure, scene, narration, reflection, description, and researched information. Craft, analysis of published literary creative nonfiction essays, workshop-style critique, multiple drafts, and substantive revision.

prerequisites.text: CCOM 200 or WCOM 203 or permission of the Centre.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CCOM 323.

subject: WCOM
title: Plurilingual Writing
description: Explores writing as a plurilingual practice through creative and academic compositions that draw on multiple linguistic resources. Examines how languages interact in meaning-making, narrative construction, and rhetorical expression. Focuses on translanguaging strategies, cross-linguistic genres, and plurilingual voice across diverse written forms.

subject: WCOM
title: Selected Communication Topic 1
description: Study of a selected topic in written and/or oral communication in English that is relevant to undergraduate students.
notes: The content can vary from year to year and will be announced prior to registration.

subject: WCOM
title: Selected Communication Topic 2
description: Study of a selected topic in written and/or oral communication in English that is relevant to undergraduate students.
notes: The content can vary from year to year and will be announced prior to registration.

subject: WCOM
title: Advanced Communicating Science
description: Use of digital platforms to produce written and oral assignments (in English) designed to communicate scientific challenges and findings to broad audiences. Rhetorical analysis of academic and popular genres including abstracts, researcher profiles, infographics, and serial and episodic podcasting.

prerequisites.text: CCOM 314 or WCOM 314 or permission of the Centre.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CCOM 414.

subject: WCOM
title: Digital Storytelling
description: Analysis and application of digital storytelling strategiesthrough the production of long-form written and spokencontent for English-language audiences. Drafting,revision, concision, precision, and digital affordances inlong-form journalism, essays, and podcasts. Topicsinclude narrative structure, character development,accessibility, socio-technical analysis, and audioproduction.

prerequisites.text: CCOM 315 or WCOM 317, or permission of the Centre

subject: WCOM
title: Business and Professional Communication
description: Written and oral communication skills in English for business and professional purposes. Concepts and principles of effective written communication. Planning, composing, editing, and polishing documents of various lengths and formats; conventions of workplace correspondence; direct and indirect approaches to workplace messages; composing routine, persuasive, positive, and negative messages; planning and delivering effective presentations, including creating effective visuals.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CCOM 550 or CESL 525; not open to students who have taken or are taking WCOM 555. Open to graduate students, and to undergraduate students in third or fourth year.

notes: WCOM 550 is designed for students with fluency in spoken and written English. Students for whom English is a second or additional language should take WCOM 555.

subject: WCOM
title: ESL: Business and Professional Communication
description: Written and oral communication skills for business and professional purposes for students whose first language is not English. Concepts and principles of effective written communication. Planning, composing, editing, and polishing documents of various lengths and formats; conventions of workplace correspondence; direct and indirect approaches to workplace messages; composing routine, persuasive, positive, and negative messages; planning and delivering effective presentations, including creating effective visuals; strategies to address common English as Second Language (ESL) errors in grammar, syntax, and vocabulary.

restrictions.text: Open to graduate students, and to undergraduate students in third or fourth year. McGill Writing Centre ESL Placement Test required for admission. Not open to students who have taken CCOM 550 or CESL 525; not open to students who have taken or are taking WCOM 550.

notes: WCOM 555 is designed for students for whom English is a second or additional language. Students whose first language is English should take WCOM 550.

subject: WCOM
title: Communicating Research to the Public
description: Production of written assignments designed to communicate complex ideas and research problems and findings to varied audiences in English. Analysis of discursive academic and policy conventions in terms of audience, purpose, organization, and style for their translation to non-specialist audiences, including the general public and/or policymakers.
notes: 1. Grading in this course is pass/fail.
2. Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop and withdrawal deadlines do not apply.

subject: WCOM
title: Communicating Research to the Digital Public
description: Production of written and oral assignments designed to communicate complex ideas and research findings through digital platforms in English. Creation of projects that may include lay audience abstracts, content creation on social media, and the production of infographics, and podcasts.
notes: Grading in this course is pass/fail.
Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop and withdrawal deadlines so not apply.

subject: WCOM
title: ESL: Strategies for Academic Communication
description: Key language learning strategies for expressing complex ideas in academic writing across the disciplines. Corpus tools to identify collocations; strategies to build productive scholarly vocabulary; self-editing techniques to avoid common English-as-Second-Language (ESL) errors in grammar, syntax and mechanics.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CESL 631.

notes: Intended for graduate students whose first language is not English.
Grading in this course is pass/fail.
Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop and withdrawal deadlines do not apply.

subject: WCOM
title: Cornerstones of Academic Writing
description: Key strategies for scholarly communication across disciplines: reading scholarly texts for structure; applying these structures in writing assignments. Four cornerstones of academic writing: audience, purpose, organization, and style. Identifying and targeting audiences, clarifying the purposes served by different writing projects, organizing ideas, and developing mastery of rhetorical and stylistic conventions.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CEAP 642. Only open to graduate students.

notes: Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop and withdrawal deadlines do not apply.
Grading in this course is pass/fail.

subject: WCOM
title: ESL: Fundamentals of Academic Writing
description: Key strategies for academic writing across disciplines: reading scholarly texts for structure; applying these structures in writing assignments; developing vocabulary building strategies; identifying and practicing nuances of scholarly English syntax. Self-editing techniques to avoid common English-as-Second-Language (ESL) errors; review of English grammar and mechanics.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CESL 641.

notes: Intended for graduate students whose first language is not English.
Grading in course is pass/fail.
Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop and withdrawal deadlines do not apply.

subject: WCOM
title: Fundamentals of Academic Presentations
description: Developing and delivering academic presentations, with emphasis on how to structure content, critically evaluate content, and use rhetorical devices to enhance clarity.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CEAP 652.

notes: Intended for graduate students.
Grading in this course is pass/fail.
Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop and withdrawal deadlines do not apply.

subject: WCOM
title: ESL: Pronunciation for Effective Communication
description: Pronunciation skills for effective communication in English about research and complex ideas in academic settings with emphasis on features of pronunciation that most affect intelligibility.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CESL 651.

notes: Intended for graduate students whose first language is not English.
Grading in this course is pass/fail.
Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop and withdrawal deadlines do not apply.

subject: WCOM
title: Literature Review 1: Summary and Critique
description: Responsible and effective engagement with other scholars’ work in order to summarize and critique research literature. Focus on economic use of language and techniques for mobilizing existing scholarship in service of an original research project.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CEAP 661.

notes: Grading in this course is pass/fail.
Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop and withdrawal deadlines do not apply.

subject: WCOM
title: Literature Review 2: Establishing Scholarly Niches
description: Situating original student research in existing scholarship through analysis of literature in a discipline; application of techniques for framing contributions.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CEAP 665.

notes: Grading in this course is pass/fail.
Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop and withdrawal deadlines do not apply.

subject: WCOM
title: Selected Topics in Communication 1
description: Study of a selected topic in written and/or oral communication relevant to postgraduates. The content can vary from year to year and will be announced prior to registration.
notes: Grading in this course is pass/fail.
Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop and withdrawal deadlines do not apply.

subject: WCOM
title: Selected Topics in Communication 2
description: Study of a selected topic in written and/or oral communication relevant to postgraduates. The content can vary from year to year and will be announced prior to registration.
notes: Grading in this course is pass/fail.
Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop and withdrawal deadlines do not apply.

subject: WCOM
title: Thesis Writing Lab
description: Writing and revising of a chapter or manuscript for structure, clarity, cohesion, and disciplinary conventions; practical strategies for writing and rewriting productively; techniques for organizing ideas and editing for flow; peer review.
notes: Grading in this course is pass/fail.
Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop and withdrawal deadlines do not apply.
For graduate students from related disciplines who are working on a thesis chapter or publishable manuscript.
Mode of delivery is online synchronous.

subject: WCOM
title: Writing for Graduate Students
description: Audience, purpose, organization, and style of graduate-level academic writing with attention to mechanics, textual analysis, critical thinking and editing skills. Common rhetorical patterns to organize research writing, including problem-solution, general-specific, process description, data commentary, article summary/critique.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken CESL 690.

notes: For graduate students only

**Due to the condensed nature of this course, the standard add/drop, and withdrawal deadlines do not apply. Add/drop is the second lecture day and withdrawal with financial penalty is the fourth lecture day.

subject: WCOM
title: ESL: Academic Writing for Graduate Students
description: Structuring an academic paper and expressing complex ideas in English using common rhetorical patterns. Academic reading, critical thinking, vocabulary building, and writing mechanics. Self-editing to enhance cohesion and avoid common English-as-a-Second Language (ESL) errors in grammar, syntax, and vocabulary.

restrictions.text: Open only to graduate students in degree programs for whom English is not their first language. Not open to students who have taken CESL 640.

notes: This course cannot be counted towards course requirements of any graduate program.
